newsitem.title: CHINA: China officials urge no more 10-year bond issues.
newsitem.headline: China officials urge no more 10-year bond issues.

text.p: China should limit issues of high-interest 10-year government bonds and issue more short-term debt, and China Reform News quoted officials as saying.

China's first issue last June of 10-year government debt with an annual coupon of 11.83 percent, or 4.36 percentage points above the interest on one-year bank deposits, had placed a considerable burden on state coffers, it quoted State Commission for Economic Restructuring officials as saying.

In addition, China's first issue with an option of compound interest was particularly attractive to individual and corporate investors because the bonds were tradeable, but underwriters preferred to retain them as assets and were reluctant to sell, the official newspaper said in its Friday edition.
The report was made available to Reuters on Sunday.

It quoted some officials as recommending such issues, which could ease the debt payment load at peak periods, but said macroeconomic experts believed there was little need for more issues before the end of 1996.
China had said it planned to issue a total of 195.4 billion yuan worth of debt this year, of which 180 billion yuan would be domestic, the newspaper said.
More than 180 billion in debt had already been issued, including 35 billion worth of short-term debt, the newspaper said.
It quoted experts as questioning whether China should issue another 35 billion of short-term debt in the second half of the year.
It estimated the annual interest on the 10-year treasury bonds at about 17 percent after taking into account interest rate cuts on May 1 and August 23 and falling inflation.
It quoted economic restructuring officials as calling for more issues of short-term debt, saying this was a necessary tool for the central bank since it began open market operations last April.

In the first half of the year, the central bank had taken part in open market operations seven times, buying back a total of 1.5 billion yuan, the newspaper said. However, since the scale was small, it had failed to have a major impact.

The newspaper said the issue of more short-term debt was necessary because, with the four big state-owned commercial banks holding only a small amount of short-term debt, if the central bank were to buy back large amounts it would create enormous price volatility.
